items.stem:
If the mean of the following data is 14.7, find the values of p and q.
Class0-66-1212-1818-2424-3030-3636-42Total
Frequency10p47q4140
items.answer:
Take class marks xᵢ = 3, 9, 15, 21, 27, 33, 39. Then Σfᵢ = 26 + p + q = 40, so p + q = 14. … (1)
Also Σfᵢxᵢ = 30 + 9p + 60 + 147 + 27q + 132 + 39 = 408 + 9p + 27q.
Mean = Σfᵢxᵢ / Σfᵢ gives 14.7 = (408 + 9p + 27q)/40, so 588 = 408 + 9p + 27q, i.e. 180 = 9p + 27q, which reduces to p + 3q = 20. … (2)
Subtracting (1) from (2): 2q = 6, so q = 3, and then p = 14 − 3 = 11.
Hence p = 11 and q = 3.

items.stem:
Find the mean and median for the following data :
Class0-1010-2020-3030-4040-50
Frequency81636346
items.answer:
Class marks are 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, so Σfᵢxᵢ = 40 + 240 + 900 + 1190 + 270 = 2640 with Σfᵢ = 100.
Mean = 2640/100 = 26.4.
The cumulative frequencies are 8, 24, 60, 94, 100. Here N = 100, so N/2 = 50; the first cumulative frequency greater than 50 is 60, so the median class is 20-30 with l = 20, F = 24, f = 36, h = 10.
Median = 20 + ((50 − 24)/36) × 10 = 20 + 7.22 = 27.22.
Hence the mean is 26.4 and the median is 27.22.

items.stem:
If the median of the following data is 240, then find the value of f :
Classes0-100100-200200-300300-400400-500500-600600-700
Frequency1517f12952
items.answer:
The cumulative frequencies are 15, 32, 32 + f, 44 + f, 53 + f, 58 + f, 60 + f, so N = 60 + f and N/2 = (60 + f)/2.
The median 240 lies in the class 200-300, so that is the median class, with l = 200, F = 32, h = 100 and frequency f.
240 = 200 + [((60 + f)/2 − 32)/f] × 100, so 40 = [(60 + f − 64)/(2f)] × 100.
This gives 8f = 10f − 40, so 2f = 40.
Hence f = 20.

The first cumulative frequency greater than 50 is 64, so the median class is 90-100 with l = 90, F = 46, f = 18, h = 10.

items.stem:
Find the mode of following data :
MarksBelow 10Below 20Below 30Below 40Below 50
Number of students820455870
items.answer:
The figures given are cumulative, so first recover the class frequencies by successive differences: 0-10 has 8, 10-20 has 12, 20-30 has 25, 30-40 has 13 and 40-50 has 12, a total of 70.
The largest frequency 25 belongs to 20-30, so that is the modal class, with l = 20, f₁ = 25, f₀ = 12, f₂ = 13, h = 10.
Mode = l + ((f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)) × h = 20 + ((25 − 12)/(50 − 12 − 13)) × 10 = 20 + (13/25) × 10 = 20 + 5.2.
Hence the mode is 25.2.

items.stem: The sum of deviations of a set of values x₁, x₂, x₃, …………, xₙ, measured from 50 is −10 and the sum of deviations of the values from 46 is 70. Find the value of n and the mean.
items.answer:
We are given Σ(xᵢ − 50) = −10 and Σ(xᵢ − 46) = 70.
Expanding, Σxᵢ − 50n = −10 … (1) and Σxᵢ − 46n = 70 … (2).
Subtracting (2) from (1): −4n = −80, so n = 20.
Putting n = 20 in (1): Σxᵢ − 1000 = −10, so Σxᵢ = 990.
Mean = Σxᵢ/n = 990/20 = 49.5.
Hence n = 20 and the mean is 49.5.

items.answer:
By definition the mean is x̄ = (1/n) Σxᵢ, so nx̄ = Σxᵢ.
Now Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = (x₁ − x̄) + (x₂ − x̄) + … + (xₙ − x̄) = (x₁ + x₂ + … + xₙ) − nx̄ = Σxᵢ − nx̄.
Since Σxᵢ = nx̄, this difference is nx̄ − nx̄ = 0.
Hence Σ(xᵢ − x̄) = 0.

items.stem:
Compute the median from the following data :
Mid-values115125135145155165175185195
Frequency62548721166038223
items.answer:
Only the mid-values are given, so the classes must be rebuilt first. Consecutive mid-values differ by h = 125 − 115 = 10, and each class runs from mid-value − h/2 to mid-value + h/2, giving 110-120, 120-130, 130-140, 140-150, 150-160, 160-170, 170-180, 180-190, 190-200.
The cumulative frequencies are 6, 31, 79, 151, 267, 327, 365, 387, 390, so N = 390 and N/2 = 195.
The first cumulative frequency greater than 195 is 267, so the median class is 150-160 with l = 150, f = 116, h = 10 and F = 151.
Median = 150 + ((195 − 151)/116) × 10 = 150 + 3.8.
Hence the median is 153.8.

items.stem: The mean of n observations is x̄, if the first term is increased by 1, second by 2 and so on. What will be the new mean ?
items.answer:
The first observation gains 1, the second gains 2, the third gains 3, and so on up to the nth observation, which gains n.
So the amount added to the total is 1 + 2 + 3 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2.
The new mean is the old mean plus this amount divided by n, that is x̄ + [n(n + 1)/2]/n.
Hence the new mean is x̄ + (n + 1)/2.

Find the mode of the following frequency distribution :
Class-Intervalf
25-357
35-4531
45-5533
55-6517
65-7511
75-851
items.answer:
The largest frequency is 33, which belongs to the class 45-55, so that is the modal class.
Here l = 45, f₀ = 31, f₁ = 33, f₂ = 17 and h = 10.
Mode = l + ((f₁ − f₀)/(2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)) × h = 45 + ((33 − 31)/(66 − 31 − 17)) × 10 = 45 + (2/18) × 10 = 45 + 1.1.
Hence the mode is 46.1.

items.stem: The mode of a distribution is 55 and the modal class is 45-60 and the frequency preceding the modal class is 5 and the frequency after the modal class is 10. Find the frequency of the modal class.
items.answer:
Here the mode is 55; the modal class 45-60 gives l = 45 and h = 15; the preceding frequency is f₁ = 5 and the succeeding frequency is f₂ = 10. Let the modal-class frequency be f.
Mode = l + ((f − f₁)/(2f − f₁ − f₂)) × h, so 55 = 45 + ((f − 5)/(2f − 5 − 10)) × 15.
Then 10 = ((f − 5)/(2f − 15)) × 15, so 10/15 = (f − 5)/(2f − 15), that is 2/3 = (f − 5)/(2f − 15).
Cross-multiplying, 4f − 30 = 3f − 15, so f = 15.
Hence the frequency of the modal class is 15.

items.stem: The sum of deviations of a set of values x₁, x₂, x₃, …………, xₙ, measured from 50 is −10 and the sum of deviations of the values from 46 is 70. Find the value of n and the mean.
items.answer:
We are given Σ(xᵢ − 50) = −10 and Σ(xᵢ − 46) = 70.
Expanding, Σxᵢ − 50n = −10 … (1) and Σxᵢ − 46n = 70 … (2).
Subtracting (2) from (1): −4n = −80, so n = 20.
Putting n = 20 in (1): Σxᵢ − 1000 = −10, so Σxᵢ = 990.
Mean = Σxᵢ/n = 990/20 = 49.5.
Hence n = 20 and the mean is 49.5.
